mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% within the last month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP by more than 2% over the last quarter signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer demand rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of quarters where GDPC1 increased by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% over the last two months signals increased economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as supply chains improve and production efficiency increases.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% over the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% within the last month, it signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 70% of instances where both PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the last month signals a weakening demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending slows and economic growth decelerates.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS decreased by more than 1% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% within the last month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns diminish.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS was above 3% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the last two months signals a strengthening construction sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and investment in the housing market increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% over the last two months.
